What changes (Save ▾ → What changes, while changes wait) runs the same check before you save and lists what changes for the pinned records ("Record 284212 loses the Zone field", "lands on another form") and the form cost against its limit. It only reads.

After each deploy the readiness scorecard (Configuration → "Pinned test records still see their forms as before") opens every pinned record the way its role would and compares it with what the previous version showed: which form it opens on, which fields it shows and which its role may edit. A difference is a warning naming the record and the change. Accept what test records see now makes the current view the one later checks compare with. Show-when rules on tabs are not judged.

Rules and checks

Rules on the canvas

The Rules switch in the top bar (the branch icon; on by default, remembered per browser) puts small tags on the canvas that say why each field behaves as it does: Required here or Required field (this form or every form), Needed to Approve (a pipeline move requires it), Read-only here, Read-only field, Calculated, Locked for Finance, Locked in Approved, Hidden here, Hidden field, and Filled by a rule. Hover a tag for the whole sentence; click it to open what causes it: the field's Rules, Look or Advanced tab, the section, the pipeline or the field rules page.

Sections carry their rules as sentences too, worded as on the overview: "Shows when Is Sparing is Yes", "Skipped when Project is filled", "Hidden for Finance", "Read-only for Finance".

Hover a field whose value decides something else: every section it shows or hides, picker it filters, field a rule fills and grid whose lines or row rules read it gets a dashed amber ring, and the field a "Controls n" tag.

Without a preview record, each input shows in grey the value a new record on this form starts with: "Default: Open" from the form's defaults, "By rule: …" when a field rule fills it from those defaults, "From Project: …" when a cross-record default copies it from a record a default picks. Yes/no and multi-pick fields show it as a tag. Nothing is saved; preview a record to see its real values instead.

Rule loops are flagged in a banner above the canvas and on the overview: a section that shows only by a field placed inside that same section (once hidden, nobody can change the field back), or fields whose rules, cascades and section rules decide each other in a circle. The fields involved get a Rule loop tag; Show selects the first one. A loop of field rules alone is the same on every form, so the overview says it once above the list.

Fields by state

States in the top bar shows every field against the states of the collection's pipeline (a switcher picks one when several run on it), with an Every state column first. Click a cell to set the field to Editable, Read-only, Required or Hidden. Every state writes the field's own Read-only, Required and Hidden on this form. Read-only in one state adds that state to the field's Read-only when. Required in one state makes the moves that leave the state ask for the value (a record-fields requirement on those moves); that is saved to the pipeline at once, for every form, and its toast has Undo. A field cannot be hidden in one state only, and a state nothing leaves cannot require anything: those choices stay greyed with the reason. A dot on a cell marks a field that is read-only but required, which nobody could fill in.

Sections by role

Roles in the top bar shows every section and tab against every role. Click a cell to make the section Can edit, Read-only or Hidden for that role (the section's Hidden for and Read-only for). Each cell is one change to save. Administrator roles are greyed: they always see and edit everything. Field permissions still apply inside a section.

How a field behaves on live records

Settings on a field that change what people see and do on a saved record. All of them are per placement (this form only) and off until you set them.

  • Label and help by state or role (Look tab): different words in a workflow state or for a role, for example "Requested date" that reads "Delivered date" once Completed. Add a rule, pick the states or roles, and type the label and help text for that case; the first rule that matches wins. The record page, the read view and the PDF follow it, and Preview as a role or a state shows it on the canvas.
  • Recommended (Rules tab): between optional and required. The field gets an amber dot beside its label; saving lists the recommended fields still empty but never stops the save. The record header counts them on their own ("2 recommended to fill"), apart from the required-fields percentage. Required wins when both are on.
  • Confirm changes on saved records (Rules tab): changing the field on an existing record asks "Are you sure?" and a short reason before the save. The reason is stored with the change and shows in the record history. Tick states to ask only while the record is in them; with none ticked it asks in every state. New records are never asked. A transition button that would save the change asks first, then you start the move again.
  • Repeat last value (Rules tab): a Repeat last button beside the label fills in what this person entered for the field on their previous record of the collection, read from their own change history. It never offers another person's value, encrypted fields or system tables.
  • Counter and limit (Look tab, text fields): a counter under the input in characters or words. The limit starts at the database column size; past the limit the form will not save. Leave the limit empty to count without one.
  • Display formula (Add panel → Display formula): a read-only figure worked out on the page from fields already on the form, for example Remaining = {{budget}} - {{committed}}, shown as plain, whole, 0.00, money or a percent. It uses the same expression language as other client formulas, is never stored and creates no computed field. The inspector flags syntax errors, names that are not fields and fields that are not on this form (they read as empty there).

Problems

The Problems count in the top bar (the alert icon and a number) counts the errors and warnings on the form as you edit it; it opens the Problems panel listing them, worst first (Errors, Warnings, Tips). Click one to select it on the canvas. Many come with a fix that is one undo step.

  • A required field the form hides, or one in a section hidden or locked for a role that can edit the record — or that must fill it to make a transition.
  • A picker that narrows its choices by a field that is not on the form.
  • Empty sections, steps and tabs holders.
  • Steps and sections no record reaches (their show-when rules can never hold, or contradict the record rules of the form, or every role but administrators is hidden from them), and fields that sit only there or are hidden everywhere they are placed.
  • Accessibility: fields without a label, a required field whose label (and so its required mark) is hidden, a half-width field that sits after a wider one although it would fit beside the field above it, and a chosen colour that reads below 3:1 on the light or dark background.

These checks are counted, never guessed. The AI review in Form settings → Tools also reads labels and help text.

Checks against the database

  • Stored as (Look tab): the database type and size behind the field, for example nvarchar(50). A warning shows when this form's default value, the input mask or the label cannot fit: a default longer than the column or past its digits, a mask that stores more characters than the column holds, or a label longer than the field's width shows.
  • Check the width against stored values (Look tab, single-line fields): reads the newest 5,000 stored values, never the whole table, and says how long 95% of them are and how much the current width shows. When the width cuts them off, or is far wider than needed, Use ⅓ (or the width it names) sets it in one Undo step.
  • Options for a record (Picker tab): pick a saved record and see the options this picker would offer it — the cascade filters and option filter worked out as the record form works them out (the draft you are editing included), then the picker exclusions — with the count left after each step and the first 50 options. When the target collection has a picker filter, the count it would leave is shown too: the record form's picker does not apply it; enforced API writes do.
  • Placements that point at nothing (overview): placements whose column was dropped, whose widget was deleted, whose grid's table or link column is gone (relations are a claim: the table and column must exist) or whose section no longer exists. Remove it / Remove N takes them off that layout in one save, with a version kept like any other edit.

Commands and AI

Type a change (⌘K)

AI → Type a change… (⌘K or Ctrl+K) takes a change in plain words. Enter shows every change it will make, in sentences; nothing changes until Apply, and one Apply is one undo step that waits for Save like any other change. Names match by label or key, in any case, with partial words and small typos; a name that fits two things asks you to be more specific.

  • move Shipping Location to Materials · move Notes after Zone · move section Details after Extras · move Notes to ungrouped
  • make Zone required · make Notes optional · make Zone read-only / editable · hide Notes · show Notes
  • rename Notes to "Comments" · rename section Details to Basics
  • set width Zone 6 · set Zone width to half · make Zone a third
  • add Region to Location (a field not on the form yet) · add step Review after Details · add section Extras
  • remove Notes (the data is kept) · collapse Extras · expand Extras
  • Several commands in one go: separate them with ";" — they apply as one change.

Required is set per form, not per role: "make Zone required for Finance" makes it required on this form and says so when the form is not limited to Finance (give Finance its own form to require it only there). Text the palette cannot read can go to the AI (admins, when AI is set up): it answers in the same commands, shown in the same preview before anything changes. Without AI the typed commands still work.

AI assists (admins)

When AI is set up, administrators get five helpers. Each one only proposes: a change lands through the draft as one undo step, and nothing is applied without Apply. The AI reads field names, labels, help text, roles and the workflow — never record values.

  • AI review (Save ▾ → AI review): after a Save the AI reads what changed next to the roles and the workflow and warns about likely mistakes, such as hiding Amount from Finance, who must fill it before Approve. It never blocks or delays the save; warnings open beside the Save menu (their count shows on its arrow) and Undo reverses a saved change. Picking AI review asks before saving. A change that only renames, rewrites help text or reorders inside a section is not sent.
  • Help text that contradicts the form (Form settings → Tools → Review this layout): help text that says "optional" while a workflow move needs the field, or names a role that cannot edit it, is flagged with a rewrite. Use the rewrite changes only the help text on this form.
  • Fields that mean the same thing (same review): two fields with different labels that hold the same information, such as Vendor and Supplier. Identical labels are a separate finding.
  • Natural entry order: an order inside each section that follows how people fill the form in (who, what, when, cost), with fields that filter or show other fields first. Apply one section or Apply all — one undo step either way.
  • Personal and financial fields: fields that look personal or financial and are seen on this form by a broad role (one holding a fifth of active people, or roles that together hold half). The suggestion hides the field's section from those roles, leaving out roles that edit the field or need it for a workflow move, and says which other fields go with it. This is advice, not a security control: the API still returns a field to every role whose permissions read it.

AI tools

The AI menu in the top bar (administrators) holds three reviews: Test as a role, Review the look and Tune from autofill. None of them changes the form by itself: every fix is shown in sentences first, and one Apply is one undo step that waits for Save like any other change. Findings appear as tags on the canvas; click one in the list to select that field or section, and Clear marks removes the tags.

  • Test as a role: pick a role (and, if you like, what that person is trying to do). The AI plays someone in that role filling in a new record, step by step, and says where they would hesitate — a confusing step, label or field — with a suggestion; a clearer label can be applied with one click. Built-in checks run even without AI: a required field the role cannot see or change (the record could not be saved), a step with nothing for them to fill in, a label that reads like a database name, two fields with the same label. Only labels, help text, choices and the form's structure are sent, never stored data. Nothing is saved.
  • Review the look: the AI reviews how the form looks — density, the order and nesting of sections, alignment of widths — and pins each comment to its section. It gets a picture of the canvas (typed values hidden) when the AI provider can read pictures; with a preview record on the canvas, or with a provider that cannot read pictures, it gets the sections' structure and measured sizes instead, and says so. Built-in checks flag long full-width stacks, ragged rows and one-field sections.
  • Tune from autofill: for collections that use "Fill from document", the fields people most often change after the AI proposed a value (last 90 days, counts only). Fields changed in at least a quarter of their proposals start ticked. "Highlight after autofill" rings those fields with a Check this tag only when the form was filled from a document; "Add Check these section" moves them into a section at the top of the form (on a steps or tabs form, a first step).

AI fill per field: in the inspector's Look tab, a text field can get its own AI fill button with a prompt. Write {{field_name}} in the prompt (or pick from Insert a field) to use another field's current value; nothing else from the record is sent. A field's own setting wins over the form-wide "AI generate buttons" switch (turned off, it hides the button on that field). Anyone who may change the field on that record can use the button — not only administrators — and fields they cannot read stay empty in the prompt. The value goes into the form like typing; it is saved with the record.

Write rules with AI

Admins with AI set up can describe a rule in words beside the setting it changes. The AI answers in the form's own rule format; names it cannot match are left out and listed. It sees field names, labels, choices and the layout — never stored values.

  • A step's "Only when" and a field's "Read-only when" → Write with AI. "Hide this step when Is Sparing is yes or Warehouse is 3" becomes conditions the step checks. Before Apply you see how many of the newest 500 records it shows on (or locks on), next to today's count. Apply is one undo step and saves with the form.
  • Steps can show and hide by a field's value; single fields cannot. A field locks by pipeline state or by role, not by another field's value. The AI says so instead of guessing.
  • Picker tab → Narrow the options → Write with AI: "only regions of the record's zone" becomes a cascade filter or an option filter. Pick a record to see its options today and with the change, side by side. Use this adds it to the field's every-form change, which you confirm.
  • Rules tab → Default for new records → Write a rule with AI: "Default Zone from the project's zone" becomes a field rule, tried on five records (now, after the rule, and what a new record gets). It is saved only when you confirm, and then runs on every form and API write.
  • Rules tab → Checks → Suggest checks: patterns, ranges and lengths learned from the values stored today, each with how many existing values it would refuse. Nothing is applied until you pick a check and confirm the every-form change. Without AI the pattern-based checks still appear.

AI wording

Form settings → Tools → AI wording (administrators) checks the words on the form. Each tool lists its changes as sentences with a checkbox; Apply sends the ticked ones through the editor as one undo step, and nothing is saved until Save. A change whose text was edited since you asked is greyed out — run the tool again.

  • Glossary terms — every label, help text and section name that uses another word for a term in the AI knowledge glossary (CAR for PUB'd), listed with where it shows, and rewritten to the term on this form.
  • Section intros — a one- or two-sentence note at the top of each step or section saying what to fill in and why. It is the section's Intro in the inspector, shown as a note or a warning.
  • Placeholders — example text for empty inputs from the shape of stored values (PO-######, typical amounts). Values never reach the AI, and an example that equals or contains a stored value is refused.
  • Choice labels — readable labels for coded choices such as $t:pending_approval or IN_PROGRESS. Per row, put them on this form only or on the field, which changes every form that uses the field's own list straight away (that one is not part of Undo).
  • Plain language — a plain-language score from 0 to 100 for every label, help text and intro, worst first, with a simpler rewrite that must score higher. Glossary terms do not count as unexplained abbreviations.
  • Translations — label and help drafts for a language set under Settings → Localization. Drafts are marked as drafts until someone approves them (Approve or Approve all); approved translations are never redrafted.

Without AI, Glossary terms, Placeholders, Choice labels and Plain language still work from rules; Section intros and Translations need AI.

Build a form with AI

Admins, when AI is set up. New form → Start with AI makes a new form; AI → Rebuild or lighter version in the editor rebuilds the open one (the same AI menu holds the reviews above). Every proposal is listed in plain sentences first. Nothing is written until Apply (or Create form), it lands as one undo step, and it still waits for Save.

  • Describe it: "a returns form with a manager approval step". The steps or sections are built from the fields this collection already has. Any name the AI makes up is left out and listed.
  • From a picture or PDF: a screenshot, scan, PDF or spreadsheet of an old form (up to 10 MB). Its labels are matched to fields, and its order and grouping are kept. Labels with no field are listed as candidate new fields. They are never created for you.
  • From a process document: one step per stage, with the passage each step came from. You also get suggested read-only fields per pipeline state (ticked) and required fields (unticked: Required counts for every state).
  • Lighter version for a role: pick a role. You see the fields its people changed in the last 180 days, and the fields it would hide. Create lighter version makes a new form that inherits from this one, is shown only to that role, and hides the unused fields.
  • Sections by meaning: at the top of the Add panel (and under AI). Each field not on the form gets a suggested section, based on what the field means. This helps on a new collection that has no usage history yet.
The AI gets field names, labels, descriptions and the form layout. It never gets record values. An uploaded file is read once and never stored. The lighter version reads only which fields were changed, never the values. If the AI rebuild leaves a step or section still holding fields, it is kept and named.

Ask about this form

AI → Ask… opens a panel on the right for questions such as "Why can't Finance see Zone on record 284212?" or "Which form does record 284212 get?". The AI answers with the same engines the editor shows: which form a record gets for a role (Test a record), the role's field permissions, where the field sits, the section rules (hidden or read-only for roles, shows when) and the checks. It reads your unsaved draft, changes nothing, and never sees record values: a section rule comes back as matched or not. Each answer lists the fields, records and forms it looked at; click one to select the field, preview the record or open the form. Administrators only; it needs AI to be set up.

Find a setting by asking

Ask "Where do I turn off comments?" in the Ask panel and it lists the matching controls, each with where it lives (Form settings section or inspector tab) and a Show me button. Show me opens that panel, selects a field or section the control applies to when it is an inspector control, switches to its tab and highlights the control. The words of the question are matched first; only when they do not place it does the AI pick from the same list. Without AI the closest word matches are shown. In Form settings, a search typed as a question, or one nothing matches, offers Look everywhere, which asks the same way.

Suggested changes from assistants

A connected assistant (Claude or ChatGPT over the MCP connector, or Claude Code) can propose changes to a form with the propose_layout_ops tool. A suggested change never changes the form: AI → Suggested changes (the count shows on AI) lists them, who sent each one and through which app, the note, and every change in plain words. Try on canvas applies it to your draft as one undo step (nothing is saved until Save, unless Autosave is on); Keep marks it applied, Take back undoes it, and Reject closes it. A suggested change that no longer fits the form says why and cannot be tried.

Across forms

The overview looks across all the forms of a collection as well as at each one. Each form carries a small sketch: its sections as blocks, its fields as bars as wide as they are on the form, steps and tabs as a strip, page cards (pipeline, comments) as thin bars. The sketch is drawn from the saved layout and changes the next time the overview loads after a save.

  • Fields labelled differently: a field that reads "Vendor" on one form and "Supplier" on another is listed with every label and the forms that use it. Pick the label to keep and every form gets it at once (one change per form, each in that form's History). The field's own label clears the label set on each form. A label hidden on purpose is left alone.
  • Near copies: two forms of the same kind that are 90% or more the same (the same fields in the same sections with the same width, label and visibility) are listed with what differs. Compare side by side opens both; Make … the parent links the copy to the other form so fields added there later appear on it too. The copy keeps every field it has: remove the ones it repeats unchanged in its editor to let changes flow through.
  • Analyze → Compare forms… puts two forms side by side, read only, each drawn as people see it. "Only here" marks fields and sections the other form lacks and "Differs" marks fields set up differently (its tip says how: section, width, label, visibility, other settings). Click a field to select it on both. List the differences gives the same as a table. Pick either side from its menu, or Swap.
  • Find a field (on every form) searches every collection by field name or label and lists each form, summary, detail, PDF or grid that places the field, with its section and width there and its label when the form changes it, including forms that inherit it from a parent. Click one to open it in the editor.

Every form at once

Every form (Tools → Every form in the editor, ⋯ → Every form on the overview) changes all layouts of the collection in one go. Each run shows a preview first: per form, what will change, what is already like that, and which forms are skipped and why. Untick a form to leave it out. A form with unsaved changes in the editor is left out until you save or discard them.

  • Retire a field: takes it off every form — its placements, the header, section summaries, the quick picker, its form default, row order and PDF cover title. The preview counts the records that still hold a value; the values stay in the database. Rules that still read the field are named, not changed.
  • One change: place a field after or before another (forms without that field are skipped and listed), set its width, make it required, read-only or hidden (or the reverse), or remove it.
  • Macros: in the editor, Every form → Macros → Record writes down every change you make until Stop; name it and keep it. Replay previews it on the collection's forms: fields are matched by name and sections by label, a position becomes "after this field", and a step that does not fit a form is skipped and listed. Your macros are your own.

Each changed form saves its own version first (its History shows "Before <the change>"), so any one form can be put back from History. Right after a run, Undo this bulk change puts every changed form back at once — except a form someone changed since, which you restore from its History.

Merging two forms

Merge two forms (⋯ → Merge two forms on the overview, or Merge into one… on a near-copies finding) folds one form into another. Pick the form to keep and the form to fold in, then Preview. What only the folded form has is added to the kept one; what only one of them has becomes a section shown just for the records (or roles) that form used to open for, as a show-when rule or a hidden-for-roles list. The kept form takes over who the folded one opened for: its record rules, roles, the default and its link name when the kept form has none.

  • The preview lists what the kept form gets, who will open the merged form and what happens to the folded one, then checks the newest 2,000 records: how many move to the merged form, how many keep it, and any that will open a different form instead.
  • Worth a look lists what the merge cannot carry exactly: two forms picked in different ways (record rules and roles), record rules with nothing in common, fields set up differently on the two (the kept form's setup wins), page cards and header fields only the folded form has.
  • The folded form is renamed "… (merged into …)" and no longer opens for any record. Its sections and fields stay, so a queue, share link or child form that opens it by id keeps working; the preview names those places.
  • Apply changes both forms as one change: each saves a named "Before merge" version first. Undo the merge puts both back; either form can also be restored on its own from its History. A form someone changed since the preview is not touched: preview again.

Change log for auditors

⋯ → Change log on the overview exports every layout change in a period as a CSV: when, the form and collection, who made it (name and email), the change note and what it did (fields and sections added, removed or moved, settings changed). Pick 30 days, 90 days, this year or two dates, and this collection or every collection; Count changes shows how many first. History keeps the newest 30 versions of each form plus every named one, so the log cannot show older changes than that.

Reusing forms and sections

  • Copy a section to another layout: drag a section from the canvas onto a form in the Forms list, or select it and use Copy to layout… in the inspector (which also reaches other collections). It lands at the end of that layout with its tabs, fields and settings. Fields already on that form stay where they are.
  • Section library: select a section and use Save to library…. Saved sections show under Add → Section library on every collection; a click adds one after the selection as one undo step. Remove one with the × beside it — forms keep their copies.
  • Layout templates: ⋯ → Save as template… in the editor saves the whole form (sections, panels, header, how it behaves). New form → Start with → Template makes a new form from one. Rules for who gets a form, defaults and links to other layouts stay behind.
  • Another collection: fields with no field of the same name get their closest match (by name or label), which you can change or set to Leave out. Step conditions, skip-if-filled, field swaps, lock conditions and grid bindings are written in the other collection's terms and are left out.
  • New form → Start with → Field list: paste names (one per line or separated by commas) or upload a CSV or text file. Names are matched to fields by name or label, with close spellings marked "?"; names with no match are left out. The form gets one section with the matched fields in that order.
  • New form from this record: Test a record on the overview, or the editor's ⋯ while previewing a record (also from a record's Edit form), makes a form with one section holding the fields that record has filled in, in field order. New form → Start with → A record does the same.

Usage: how a form is used

Turn on Show how full each field is (the Usage tab, or Tools) and each field on the canvas shows how often it is filled across the collection's records ("62% filled"; under 10% its tip says it is rarely filled). It is off until you turn it on, and remembered per browser. The Add panel shows the same figure under each field ("filled on 3%"). The numbers are the Table Editor's Field usage figures and refresh every five minutes.

The record form records one small event each time someone closes it: which form, which record, how long they spent on each step, whether they saved, and, for a new record, the step they left it on without creating it. Design mode records nothing.

  • Edit form on a record page adds how many people used this form on how many records today (UTC day) to its banner.
  • The editor's Usage tab shows today's opens, people and records; the last 30 days' opens, saves and new records left unfinished; the average time on each step with how many new records were left on it; and the fields changed most often within 24 hours of a record being created (last 90 days; on records opened with this form once 20 of them are known, otherwise across the collection).
  • Suggested sections: fields people change in the same save (Jaccard over the last 90 days of revisions) that sit in different sections. Move into (the section) moves the strays next to the others in one step, which Undo reverses. Not now hides a suggestion until the editor reopens.
  • Rarely opened sections: the form also counts, per visit, each section it showed and whether the person opened it (expanded it, clicked or typed in it). A section that starts open and was opened on 10% of visits or fewer (at least 20 visits) is suggested to start collapsed; the first section of the form or of a step is never suggested, nor any section on an accordion form. Start them collapsed is one change, which Undo reverses.

A/B test two versions of a form

At the bottom of the Usage tab, Start test shows a new version of this form to half of one role: pick the role and either a copy of this form (it opens so you can change it) or another form of the collection that is not the default. Each person lands in the same half every time (a stable hash of their id), administrators always get the original, and a link name (?layout=) still opens either version. The new version never wins on its own: it only stands in for the original, so the overview lists it right after the original with an A/B pill, and Test a record shows the split.

The test compares the halves side by side: people in each half, visits, saves and save rate, average time from opening the form to saving, new records left unfinished, and records created by people in each half with how many were edited again within a day. The better side of each line is in bold once each half has 20 visits. End test asks which version everyone should get: Keep the original simply stops the test; Use the new version copies its sections, fields and settings onto the original (its name, link name and who gets it stay), so links and history are kept and History can put it back.

Usage is kept per form per day (nivaro_layout_usage_daily, nivaro_layout_usage_seen) and deleted after 180 days by the nightly layout-usage-prune job. Only counts are stored; people and records are counted, never listed.

Searches that found nothing

When someone searches a relation picker on a record form and finds nothing, the form sends the words they typed when the picker closes. The server counts them per form and field for 14 days (in Redis); it never stores who typed them or on which record. Design mode sends nothing.

Select the field in the editor and open its Picker tab: Searches that found nothing lists the top ten, how many times each was typed, and a suggested fix for the top five — the field's option filter leaves matching records out (loosen it), the picker filter or hidden records leave them out, or nothing matches at all (add the record, or turn on Quick create). Clear list empties it for that field.

Suggestions, dependencies and environments

Suggested changes from people

People who are not administrators get Suggest a form change in a record's More menu. They say what should change and can name a field. The suggestion becomes a Form change support request, so they follow it under My requests and it also shows on the Support desk. The overview's subtitle shows how many suggested changes are open and, on a click, for which forms. In the editor, Form settings → Tools → Suggested changes · from people lists them; Accept marks the request done and Decline cancels it, each with an optional note the person is told about. To turn suggestions off, deactivate the Form change type under Support → Request types. One person can send 10 suggestions an hour.

What relies on a layout

A diagram shows everything that opens a layout: other layouts, queues, grids and drill-downs, share links and public forms, generated files and extension code. Each box says whether it finds the layout by its id or its link name. Before you delete a layout, change its link name or change its kind, the diagram turns red for what that change would break. Renaming keeps every link working. Open it from the row menu (What relies on this…) or Form settings → Tools.

Extension code cannot be read for layout names, so extensions declare what they open with ctx.layouts?.dependsOn({ collection, slug | layout_id, label }) in register(). The diagram says so when no extension declares anything, rather than claiming nothing uses the layout.

Compare with another environment

Row menu → Compare with another environment (or Form settings → Tools) reads another environment's copy of this layout and lists what would change here: settings, sections and tabs, fields and order. The other copy comes from an API in the Environments registry (read by this server with that component's token), or from an uploaded file: Download this layout on the other side, or a Config Diff snapshot. The copy is matched by link name, then by name, and you can pick another. Apply here saves a version of this layout first, so History → Restore undoes it. Which layout is the default and its place in the list stay as they are here. Settings that cannot be carried (a template or layout this environment does not have, a name already taken, a value this instance refuses) are listed and left alone. Nothing is ever sent from here to the other environment.

Help, notes and the form map

  • Help videos on a field or section: a field's Help tab, or the bottom of a section's inspector, attaches a published help video. The record page then shows a small play button beside that field's label or on that section's header, to the roles the video is visible to. The attachment belongs to the video (it appears in its Where list), so it shows for that field or section on every form of the collection.
  • Notes for editors: pin a short note to a field (Help tab) or a section (bottom of its inspector), such as "Finance asked for this in Q3". A sticky-note marker shows on the canvas with the note, its author and date. Notes save, undo and version like any other layout change, and record pages never receive them.
  • Form map (Tools → Form map): a clean printable map of the form: its steps or tabs, sections and fields in order, each field's width, required and read-only marks, and the rules that hide or lock things, in plain words. Print / Save as PDF prints it on a light page whatever the app theme.
  • Why can't I edit this? On a record, pointing at a locked field names the exact rule behind it: the role or pipeline step a lock rule lists, the section locked for the role and the form it is on, or the role's field permissions. Admins also see a "N fields hidden by rules" note above the form that lists each hidden field and the rule that hides it (step rules, sections hidden from roles, fields turned off on the form).

Owner, watching and sharing a form

  • Watch: ⋯ → Watch this form in the editor top bar. While it is on you get a notification (your Profile → Notification rules decide the channels, category Watch) whenever someone saves a change to the form or restores one of its versions. It says who saved, what changed in counts (for example "2 fields moved, 1 section added") and the version note, and opens the editor with History showing. You never hear about your own saves. A watch is listed with your other notification subscriptions, where you can also remove it.
  • Owner: Share → Owner names the business owner of a form. The overview shows "Owner: …" under the form. The owner hears about every saved change even without watching, and is told first; change requests about the form go to the owner first too.
  • Review reminder: Share → Review reminder sets how long a form may stay unchanged before its owner is asked to review it: 3, 6 or 12 months, never, or the default (6 months). The reminder arrives on a weekday morning (category Watch) with the form's health score and its last 30 days of use (visits, people, saves, new records left unfinished), and comes again every that many months while the form stays unchanged. Any saved change starts the count over.
  • Preview link: Share → Preview link makes a read-only link that lasts 7, 14, 30 or 90 days, for people who are not administrators. It shows the last saved version of the form, with only the fields you may read, and never shows record data. Anyone with the link can leave a comment on a field or on the whole form; comments appear under Share → Comments from previews (the count shows on the Share button), where Select this field finds the field on the canvas and Resolve removes the comment. Turn off ends a link for everyone.

What's new on this form

The first time someone opens a record form after it changed, a short note at the top of the form lists what is new, what moved to another section and what is no longer on the form, with who changed it and when. It only names fields that person may read. Dismissing it hides it for that person until the next change; the person who saved the change never sees it, and nothing shows the very first time someone opens a form.

React to form changes in flows and webhooks

Every saved change fires the flow trigger Form Layout Changed (layout.updated), so a flow can, for example, post the change to a Teams channel. Webhooks receive it when they name the source Form layouts (saved changes): the delivery is an update event whose data carries event: "layout.updated".

// layout.updated payload (flow trigger data; webhook body data)
{
  "layout_id": 12, "layout_name": "Purchase order", "collection": "orders",
  "op_summary": "2 fields moved, 1 section added", "op_count": 3,
  "note": "Group the dates",            // the version note, or null
  "user_id": "…", "user_name": "Ada Lovelace",
  "history_url": "https://…/data-model/orders?tab=groups&layout=12&history=1"
}

Instances whose layouts are replaced

Layout configuration travels one way: development → staging every night (promote:config copies the layout, section and placement tables), staging → production at go-live. An edit made on staging is therefore gone the next morning. Set LAYOUT_EDIT_WARNING on such an instance and every layout editing surface — the overview, the editor and record-page Edit form — shows it as an always-visible banner. Unset = no banner. The editor still works either way.

# staging .env
LAYOUT_EDIT_WARNING=Layouts here are replaced every night from development. Make lasting changes on development.

API

Layout writes are admin-only. The older endpoints (PATCH a layout, PUT all placements, the field-groups routes) keep working for scripts; the editor uses the bundle + ops pair.

# Which form a record gets, checks and health (administrators)
GET  /api/collection-layouts/overview?collection=orders
     → { data: { rows: [...], warning: string | null } }   // sectioned, in /active order
GET  /api/collection-layouts/explain?collection=orders&item=42[&role_id=<uuid>][&slug=x]
     → { data: { layout_id, reason, checked: [{ layout_id, matched, why }] } }
GET  /api/collection-layouts/lint-context?collection=orders
     → { data: { fields, roles, requirements } }   // what the Problems panel reads
GET  /api/collection-layouts/health?collection=orders
     → { data: { rows: [{ layout_id, score, costs, counts, unreachable_fields }] } }
GET  /api/collection-layouts/coverage?collection=orders[&fresh=1]
     → { data: { sampled, limit, no_form, rule_error, rows: [{ layout_id, records, rule_matches }] } }
GET  /api/collection-layouts/field-access?collection=orders
     → { data: { roles: [{ role: { id, name, admin_access }, can_read, can_update,
                           hidden_fields, readonly_fields }] } }   // every role's field permissions
GET  /api/collection-layouts/:id/dependencies
     → { layout, groups, nodes, extensions }   // what relies on the layout

# Create, read and change a layout (administrators)
POST /api/collection-layouts  { collection, name, layout_type?, slug?, seed_fields?: true | string[],
                                template_id?, field_map? }
     // seed_fields: one section "Main" holding every visible field ("Create first form"),
     // or exactly the named fields in that order; template_id: a saved form template
     // (field_map renames its fields, { source: target | null })
GET  /api/collection-layouts/:id/bundle
     → { layout, groups, placements, rev }
POST /api/collection-layouts/:id/ops  { ops: LayoutOp[], base_rev, note?, reason?, ticket? }
     → the new bundle (applied all or nothing, at most 5000 ops)
     409 { error: 'stale', bundle }       // someone saved since base_rev
     400 { error, op_index }              // an op was refused (also a rename onto a taken name)
     400 { error, code: 'CHANGE_NOTE_REQUIRED' }   // the layout's change_note asks for a reason (+ ticket)
POST /api/field-config/:collection/project  { assignments: [...] }
     // the field rows GET /field-config would return if these placements were saved
     // (read-only: the canvas renders unsaved drafts through it; flushes no cache, pushes nothing)
Socket (live operations topic): ops:join { topic: 'layout:<id>' }
     ops:signal { topic, kind: 'select', state: 'start' | 'stop', target: '<design target key>' }
     ← ops:changed { topic, viewers: [{ id, name, selected? }] }   // who has the layout open

# History and scheduled changes (administrators)
GET   /api/collection-layouts/:id/versions/:versionId/bundle   → { data: { bundle, version } }
PATCH /api/collection-layouts/:id/versions/:versionId  { name | null }   // named: kept beyond the 30
POST  /api/collection-layouts/:id/versions/name  { name }   // name the layout as saved now
GET   /api/collection-layouts/:id/section-changes
      → { data: { [section key]: { by, by_id, at } } }   // who last changed each section
GET   /api/collection-layouts/schedules?collection=orders[&layout_id=5]
      → { data: [{ id, layout_id, run_at, status, op_count, created_by_name, note, error }] }
POST  /api/collection-layouts/:id/schedules  { ops, base_rev, run_at, note? }
PATCH /api/collection-layouts/schedules/:sid  { run_at }   // pending only
DELETE /api/collection-layouts/schedules/:sid              // cancel (or dismiss a failed one)

# Test records and the new-record walkthrough (administrators; read only)
POST /api/collection-layouts/:id/test-records
     { records: [{ item, role_id? }], draft?: { record_conditions, conditions, is_active, sort, layout_type }, fields?: [...] }
     → { data: { results: [{ item, role_id, found, role, saved: { layout_id, name, why }, draft: {...},
                             values: { <field>: value }, access }] } }   // at most 10 records
POST /api/collection-layouts/:id/walkthrough-access  { role_id?, draft? }
     → { data: { role, role_may_open, can_create, create_fields, hidden_fields,
                 new_record_form: { layout_id, name, why }, column_defaults } }

# Inspector reads (administrators; read only)
GET  /api/layout-inspect/:collection/columns
     → { data: { <column>: { type, max_length, precision, scale, nullable } } }
GET  /api/layout-inspect/:collection/value-lengths?field=code
     → { data: { field, sampled, filled, p50, p95, max, capped } }   // newest 5,000 rows by id
GET  /api/layout-inspect/:collection/form-fields
     → { data: [{ layout_id, name, layout_type, fields: [...] }] }
GET  /api/layout-inspect/:collection/orphans
     → { data: [{ layout_id, name, layout_type, placements: [{ field, group_key, reason }] }] }
     // reason: column_dropped | widget_deleted | grid_missing | section_missing
GET  /api/layout-inspect/:collection/translations
     → { data: { base, locales, groups_supported, layouts: [{ layout_id, name, missing, total }] } }
POST /api/layout-inspect/picker-preview
     { collection: <target>, steps: [{ key, label, filter }], fields?, sort? }
     → { data: { total, steps: [{ key, label, count, applies }], excluded, offered,
                 picker_filter, with_picker_filter, rows } }
GET  /api/widgets-internal/:id/placements
     → { data: [{ layout_id, name, collection }] }   // every layout placing the widget

# Every form at once (administrators)
GET  /api/collection-layouts/bulk/fields?collection=orders
     → { data: [{ field, forms }] }   // every field placed on a form, with how many forms hold it
POST /api/collection-layouts/bulk/preview  { collection, action, labels?, layout_ids? }
     → { data: { label, forms: [{ layout_id, name, rev, status: 'change'|'same'|'skip',
                                  reason, changes, notes }], values } }
     // action: { kind: 'retire', field }
     //       | { kind: 'change', change: { type: 'place_after'|'place_before', field, anchor }
     //                                 | { type: 'set_width', field, width: 12|6|4|3 }
     //                                 | { type: 'set_flag', field, flag: 'required'|'readonly'|'hidden', on }
     //                                 | { type: 'remove', field } }
     //       | { kind: 'macro', name, steps }
     // values (retire only): { populated, total, note } — records that still hold a value
POST /api/collection-layouts/bulk/apply  { …same, revs: { [layout_id]: rev } }
     → { data: { label, forms: [{ layout_id, status: 'applied'|'same'|'skipped'|'failed',
                                  reason, version_id, rev }] } }
     // a form whose rev moved since the preview is skipped
POST /api/collection-layouts/bulk/undo  { collection, items: [{ layout_id, version_id, rev }] }
     // restores each form unless it changed since the bulk change
GET  /api/collection-layouts/macros              // your own macros
POST /api/collection-layouts/macros  { id?, name, collection, steps, source_layout_id? }
POST /api/collection-layouts/macros/:id/delete

# Merging two forms + the change log (administrators)
POST /api/collection-layouts/merge/preview  { collection, keep_id, fold_id }
     → { data: { keep: { id, name, rev }, fold: { id, name, rev }, changes, assignment, retire, notes,
                 counts, references, needs_note,
                 records: { sampled_newest, names, views: [{ label, plain, kept, carried, lost, gained }] } } }
POST /api/collection-layouts/merge/apply  { collection, keep_id, fold_id, revs: { keep, fold }, reason?, ticket? }
     → { data: { keep: { layout_id, version_id, rev }, fold: { layout_id, version_id, rev } } }
     // 409 when either form changed since the preview; the folded form is put back if the kept one fails
POST /api/collection-layouts/merge/undo  { collection, keep: { layout_id, version_id, rev }, fold: { … } }
GET  /api/collection-layouts/change-log?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&collection=&format=csv
     → { data: { rows: [{ at, collection, layout_id, layout, version, who, who_email, note, summary, … }], truncated } }
     // format=csv downloads the same rows; at most 366 days and 5,000 changes

# Across forms (administrators)
GET  /api/collection-layouts/crossform?collection=
     → { data: { thumbs: { <layout id>: { blocks, more } }, labels: [{ field, field_label, variants }],
                 duplicates: [{ a, b, similarity, identical, only_a, only_b, differing, parent_id, can_link }] } }
GET  /api/collection-layouts/field-search?q=&collection=   // q at least 2 characters
